name: MonarchHeatmap
title: Heatmap
wrapsNative: Swift Charts RectangleMark with chartOverlay(_:) and SpatialTapGesture, inside MonarchChartFrame
summary: A matrix of values as shaded cells, such as activity by weekday and hour, with a Less to More legend.
whenToUse: To show where values cluster across two categories, such as weekday by hour or team by week.
whenNotToUse: To compare exact values, use a table or MonarchBarList. For one value per calendar day over months, use a calendar heatmap.
api: MonarchHeatmap.init(_ title: String, rows: [MonarchHeatmapAxisItem], columns: [MonarchHeatmapAxisItem], cells: [MonarchHeatmapCell], description: String? = nil, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = .ready, color: MonarchChartColor = .data1, thresholds: [Double]? = nil, showsValues: Bool = false, showsLegend: Bool = true, summary: String? = nil, emptyMessage: String? = nil, footer: String? = nil, labels: MonarchHeatmapLabels = MonarchHeatmapLabels(), formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = nil, onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onSelect: (@MainActor (MonarchHeatmapCell) -> Void)? = nil)
MonarchHeatmapAxisItem.init(_ label: String, key: String? = nil)
MonarchHeatmapCell.init(row: String, column: String, value: Double?, valueLabel: String? = nil, note: String? = nil)

MonarchHeatmapLabels.init(frame: MonarchChartFrameLabels = MonarchChartFrameLabels(), rowHeader: String? = nil, less: String? = nil, more: String? = nil, noData: String? = nil, rangeBelow: String? = nil, range: String? = nil, rangeAbove: String? = nil, size: String? = nil, rowCountOne: String? = nil, rowCount: String? = nil, columnCountOne: String? = nil, columnCount: String? = nil, highest: String? = nil, cell: String? = nil)

options.name: title
options.description: The name of the chart, shown as the frame's heading.

options.name: cells
options.description: The values in any order. A row and column pair without a cell is no data.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title, such as the period.

options.name: status
options.description: ready, loading, empty or error. A ready chart without any value shows the empty state.

options.name: color
options.description: The data colour of the steps.

options.name: thresholds
options.description: Three ascending values where levels 2, 3 and 4 start. Quarters of the largest value when nil.

options.name: showsValues
options.description: Writes each value in its cell when the cell is at least 24 points (scaled with Dynamic Type).

options.name: showsLegend
options.description: Shows the Less to More legend under the matrix.

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the generated summary that VoiceOver reads for the matrix.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The message of the empty state.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart, such as the source.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the frame's. Sentences with values are formats with %1$@ placeholders.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes a value. The default is a number in the environment's locale.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Runs with the tapped cell, or the cell selected with VoiceOver; its value is nil when it has no data.

states.name: ready
states.description: Square cells in five levels: the muted background for zero, four mixes of the data colour, and an outlined empty cell for no data.

states.name: cell selected
states.description: A tapped cell gets a default-text outline, and its row, column and value are written under the matrix.

states.name: values shown
states.description: Values are written in cells with room; on the two strongest levels they sit on a surface chip.

states.name: table
states.description: View as table lists one row per heatmap row and one column per heatmap column, with notes.

states.name: empty
states.description: The frame's empty state, also when the chart is ready but has no value.

states.name: error
states.description: The frame's error message, with Try again when onRetry is given.

appearance: Levels mix the chosen data colour into the muted background at a quarter, half, three quarters and in full; zero is the muted background and no data is a subtle-border outline on the surface. Axis labels and the legend are muted text; a selected cell is outlined in default text. The mix is computed from the theme's roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes keep five distinct steps.
platformNotes: The web Heatmap shows a tooltip on hover and moves an active cell with the arrow keys; on iOS a tap selects a cell and its details are written under the matrix, and VoiceOver moves through the cells by swiping up and down. The web mixes colours in OKLab; here the mix is per sRGB channel, so middle steps differ slightly in hue. The web maxCellSize and gap props are fixed here (36 points, a small gap), the controlled activeCell is not offered, and the legend is not a separate public view. Column labels that do not fit are dropped by Swift Charts instead of the web's measured spacing. Android uses the same names. Several closures are optional (formatValue, onRetry, onSelect). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is formatValue.
accessibility: The matrix is one element labelled with the generated summary (its size and its highest cell) or the summary given.
It is adjustable: swiping up and down visits the cells row by row and its value reads the current cell as row, column and value with its note.
With onSelect it has the button trait and a double tap selects the current cell.
It carries an AXChartDescriptor for Audio Graphs: the columns along the x axis, one series per row, cells without data left out.
The legend is one element named Legend whose value lists each step's range, so the shades are not the only key.
The frame title is a heading, and View as table lists every value as text.
Axis labels, values and the legend scale with Dynamic Type; values show only in cells large enough for the scaled text.
edgeCases: Cells for keys that are not in rows or columns are ignored.
Two cells for the same position: the later one wins.
Negative values are level 0; values that are not finite are no data.
When every value is zero or less, every positive threshold is zero and any later positive value is level 1.
Many columns make cells narrow; Swift Charts drops column labels that would overlap.
A value is written in its cell only when the cell is at least 24 points at the current text size.

examples.title: Fixed thresholds, values in cells, selectable
examples.code:
MonarchHeatmap(
    "Hours logged",
    rows: [MonarchHeatmapAxisItem("Design"), MonarchHeatmapAxisItem("Platform")],
    columns: [MonarchHeatmapAxisItem("W1"), MonarchHeatmapAxisItem("W2"), MonarchHeatmapAxisItem("W3")],
    cells: [
        MonarchHeatmapCell(row: "Design", column: "W1", value: 32),
        MonarchHeatmapCell(row: "Design", column: "W2", value: 38),
        MonarchHeatmapCell(row: "Platform", column: "W3", value: 41, valueLabel: "41h"),
    ],
    color: .data2,
    thresholds: [10, 25, 40],
    showsValues: true,
    onSelect: { selected = "\($0.row) \($0.column)" }
)
